glosses: Able to be done without; easily replaced.

examples.text: The reward could be a preferred food, a sticker, blowing some bubbles, a noisemaker the child enjoys, a pat on the back, or some other easily dispensable reward that does not take the child away from the task at hand for more than a moment or two.

glosses: Subject to dispensation; possible to relax, exempt from, or annul.

examples.text: Jones' use of the term 'Ecclesiastical Law' in his definition of dispensations in Roman Catholic canon law points to the Roman Catholic distinction between divine law, from which no dispensation is possible, and merely ecclesiastical law, which is dispensable in certain circumstances.

glosses: Not essential to be taken in as part of an organism's diet, as it can be synthesized de novo.

examples.text: The difference in absorption rate is not surprising since whey has a high percentage of indispensable amino acids, which are absorbed more rapidly than dispensable amino acids.

glosses: Something that can reasonably be dispensed with; something unnecessary.
Superfluous; exceeding what is necessary, no longer needed.

examples.text: It is allowed, that Senates and great Councils are often troubled with redundant, ebullient, and other peccant Humours, with many Diſeaſes of the Head and more of the Heart; […]

glosses: Repetitive or needlessly wordy.

examples.text: Four employees were made redundant.

glosses: Duplicating or able to duplicate the function of another component of a system, providing backup in the event the other component fails.

examples.text: The two lines are mainly used for redundant and therefore fault-tolerant message transmission, but they can also transmit different messages.

glosses: Containing duplicate pathways to send a message.
Without use or possibility to be used.

examples.text: This fork's prongs are bent. It's useless now.

glosses: Unhelpful, not useful; pointless (of an action).

examples.text: I think it's useless to keep this discussion going. It's like talking to a brick wall.
I tried my best to make him quit smoking, but my efforts were useless. He now smokes six packs a day.

glosses: Good-for-nothing; not dependable.

examples.text: Bill never mows the lawn, takes out the trash or anything. He's useless, but I love him anyways.

glosses: Unable to do well at a particular task or thing. Useless is mildly insulting.

examples.text: My brother is useless at most computer games, but he is an awesome PS2 player.
Why do you keep trying? You're obviously useless at it.

glosses: In excess of what is required or sufficient.

examples.text: With a full rain suit, carrying an umbrella may be superfluous.

Then I began to play in timid fashion, venturing only twenty or thirty gulden at a time. Meanwhile, I observed and took notes. It seemed to me that calculation was superfluous, and by no means possessed of the importance which certain other players attached to it, even though they sat with ruled papers in their hands, whereon they set down the coups, calculated the chances, reckoned, staked, and—lost exactly as we more simple mortals did who played without any reckoning at all.
